audits.title: A multi-district audit of the management of HIV infection in pregnant women and the prevention of mother-to-child transmission: Yorkshire HIV pregnancy audit.
audits.standard: British HIV Association guidelines for management of HIV infection in pregnancy

cycle1.result: 20/22 mothers received therapy as recommended; 16/22 (73%) elective caesarean; 12/22 (55%) definitely received intravenous zidovudine in delivery; 19/22 infants received appropriate antiretrovirals for four to six weeks.

audits.other_findings: No mother-to-child transmission; two mothers initially received inappropriate dual therapy; no mothers known to have breast-fed.
audits.citation: Brady SK, Monteiro EF. A multi-district audit of the management of HIV infection in pregnant women and the prevention of mother-to-child transmission: Yorkshire HIV pregnancy audit. Int J STD AIDS. 2005;16(10):712-714. doi:10.1258/095646205774357316. PMID: 16212723.

audits.title: Optimal management of HIV-infected women during pregnancy and delivery: an audit of compliance with recommendations.
audits.standard: Local recommendations for HIV-infected women in pregnancy and delivery
audits.setting: Large public university hospital, CHU Saint-Pierre, Brussels

cycle1.result: Recommendations followed in two thirds of deliveries (n = 140) with undetectable viral load and uninfected newborn.

audits.intervention: Protocol adapted: earlier antiviral therapy and nurses assigned to patient follow-up.
audits.other_findings: Two newborns infected among deliveries where optimal conditions were not met.
audits.citation: Vandermaelen A, Barlow P, Manigart Y, Hainaut M, Goetghebuer T, Levy J, et al.. Optimal management of HIV-infected women during pregnancy and delivery: an audit of compliance with recommendations. J Womens Health (Larchmt). 2009;18(11):1881-1887. doi:10.1089/jwh.2008.1167. PMID: 19951226.

audits.title: Improvement in Perinatal HIV Status Documentation in a Massachusetts Birth Hospital, 2009-2013.
audits.standard: Universal prenatal HIV testing; aim to improve documentation from 50% to 100%
audits.setting: Perinatal facility, Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, Boston, Massachusetts
audits.intervention: Three-pronged intervention: switch to verbal-only consent, rapid HIV testing protocol, simplified newborn admission document
audits.other_findings: Before intervention, mothers from freestanding offices and privately insured mothers were less likely to have status documented; in 2013 neither predicted documentation. 100 charts audited per month.
audits.citation: Paydar-Darian N, Pursley DM, Haviland MJ, Mao W, Golen T, Burris HH. Improvement in Perinatal HIV Status Documentation in a Massachusetts Birth Hospital, 2009-2013. Pediatrics. 2015;136(1):e234-41. doi:10.1542/peds.2014-3849. PMID: 26055851.

audits.title: Prevention of mother-to-child transmission in HIV audit in Xhosa clinic, Mahalapye, Botswana.

cycle1.result: 19% knew HIV-positive status; 69% seen at 14-28 weeks' gestation; 67% took antiretrovirals; 39/44 (89%) infants HIV DNA PCR negative at 6 weeks; 32 (73%) given cotrimoxazole prophylaxis at 6-8 weeks.

audits.other_findings: Service delivery was suboptimal; daily monitoring to track eligible patients was proposed.
audits.citation: Tshitenge S, Citeya A, Ganiyu A. Prevention of mother-to-child transmission in HIV audit in Xhosa clinic, Mahalapye, Botswana. Afr J Prim Health Care Fam Med. 2014;6(1):E1-4. doi:10.4102/phcfm.v6i1.609. PMID: 26245408.

audits.title: UK national clinical audit: management of pregnancies in women with HIV.
audits.setting: UK HIV services, with data from the National Study of HIV in Pregnancy and Childhood

cycle1.result: 99% of 112 services used dedicated multidisciplinary teams (26% with no specialist midwife or nurse); 17% reported delays >1 week for specialist review; ART started in pregnancy in 37% with >94% of regimens guideline-compliant; 11% of services had local delivery-mode policy contrary to guidelines.

audits.other_findings: Late ART initiation was common, especially with low CD4 count or high viral load; delays >2 h for urgent HIV results were common.
audits.citation: Raffe S, Curtis H, Tookey P, Peters H, Freedman A, Gilleece Y, et al.. UK national clinical audit: management of pregnancies in women with HIV. BMC Infect Dis. 2017;17(1):158. doi:10.1186/s12879-017-2255-6. PMID: 28219333.

audits.title: Audit of prevention of mother-to-child transmission programme interventions in HIV-Exposed children at national hospital, Abuja, Nigeria.
audits.standard: 2010 Nigerian national guideline on prevention of mother-to-child transmission of HIV

cycle1.result: MTCT in 22 (3.2%); PCR testing in 445 (64.7%); breastfeeding 402 (58.2%); post-exposure ARV prophylaxis about 88.0%; co-trimoxazole prophylaxis only 226 (34.6%).

audits.other_findings: Maternal HAART and infant PEP were independently associated with lower transmission.
audits.citation: Mukhtar-Yola M, Otuneye AT, Mairami AB, Wey Y, Nwatah V, Audu LI. Audit of prevention of mother-to-child transmission programme interventions in HIV-Exposed children at national hospital, Abuja, Nigeria. Niger Postgrad Med J. 2018;25(1):27-31. doi:10.4103/npmj.npmj_151_17. PMID: 29676342.
